title: fix(core, app-shell): an action param dialog keeps the typed input when the server refuses the run
body:
Fixes #13161

Clause-②: yes

An action's param dialog now keeps what the admin typed when the server refuses the run. It stays open and busy until the run settles, closes on success, and on a refusal keeps every value and shows the refusal above the buttons, so the admin can fix the input and confirm again, or cancel.

## What changed

- **`@object-ui/core`**: `ParamCollectionHandler` gains an optional fourth argument, `run`. Called with the collected values, it dispatches the action and resolves with that run's `ActionResult` (a dispatch that throws resolves as a refused run, as `execute` reports one).
  - A refused attempt gets its post-execution (error toast, `onFailure`) at once.
  - A successful attempt's post-execution (success toast, result dialog, chain, `onSuccess`) waits until the handler settles, so the dialog is closed before any of it shows.
  - A `run` call while one is in flight returns that run and dispatches nothing new.
  - Once `run` was called, the handler's own answer only ends the session. `null` after a refusal is a cancel.
  - A handler that never calls `run` keeps the old contract: one dispatch with the values it resolves.
  - `execute`'s dispatch tail (update operation, registered handler, builtin, legacy fallbacks) moved unchanged into the private `dispatchCollected`, so the lone run and the session share it.
- **`@object-ui/app-shell`**: `ActionParamDialog` runs the action from inside the dialog when its state carries `run`.
  - While the run is in flight, Confirm (spinner, `aria-busy`) and Cancel are disabled and the dialog refuses to close.
  - On success it settles with the values that ran, then closes.
  - On a refusal it keeps the values and shows the run's own `error` in a `role="alert"` block above the footer, outside the scrolling region.
  - Both runner-fed hosts forward `run`: `useConsoleActionRuntime` and `RecordDetailView`.

## The PM hypotheses, as measured

- **H1, holds.** `handleSubmit` called `state.resolve` and then `onOpenChange(false)`. The runner's `execute` awaited the handler, then dispatched and post-executed, so the refusal toast came after the dialog had closed. The runner is the only caller of the param handler (one call site, in `execute`). Every console param dialog renders this one component, mounted three times:
  - `useConsoleActionRuntime`, feeding the runner for ConsoleShell, ObjectView, PageView and `DeclaredActionsBar`;
  - `RecordDetailView`, which feeds the runner from its own runtime;
  - `MetadataTypeActions`, which has no runner and runs its own fetch.
- **H2, shape (a), through the runner.** A fix inside `@object-ui/app-shell` alone was measured unsound, for two reasons:
  - The glue could correlate its own `api`, `flow`, `script` and `modal` handlers with the dialog through the dispatch object. But an `operation: 'update'` action (`executeUpdateOperation`) and the builtin executors never reach a glue handler, so their dialog would hang open.
  - After a refusal the glue cannot re-dispatch, because `execute` has already returned.

  Shape (b), a runner loop that re-opens the dialog, would have to be opt-in: the in-repo handler doubles that resolve fixed values (`ActionRunner.declaredPatch-13022`, the `action-*` suites in components) would loop forever on a persistent refusal. That opt-in would itself be a type change, and the dialog would flicker closed and back open. So the narrowest widening is the one optional `run` argument.
- **H3, measured in the producers' source: none of the three refusals names a field.**
  - "Either email or phoneNumber is required": the objectstack plugin-auth `badRequest` sends `{ success: false, error: { code: 'INVALID_REQUEST', message } }`.
  - "User already exists. Use another email.": better-auth's `APIError.from` sends `{ message, code }`.
  - The redirect-URL refusal: better-call's endpoint rethrows its `ValidationError` as `APIError(400, { message, code: 'VALIDATION_ERROR' })` and drops the zod `issues`, so the path survives only inside the sentence.

  Every console handler also flattens a refusal to `ActionResult.error` (text). So the dialog marks no field. The refusal is the form's, and a field named inside the sentence is not read (pinned with the redirect-URL sentence). The wire was not re-measured in a browser.
- **H4, holds.** Cancel after a refusal settles `null`, closes and dispatches nothing more (the dialog pin, and the runner pin: one dispatch, one toast). Success closes, then toasts, exactly as before (the runner pin orders the toasts `error`, `success`, and the console pin ends on the success toast).
- **H5.** The ablation is below.

## Published face

Clause-② is `yes`, measured. The only face that moves is `@object-ui/core`'s `dist/actions/ActionRunner.d.ts`, read after the closure build:

- the `ParamCollectionHandler` line gains `run?`, a function from the values (a Record of string to any) to a Promise of `ActionResult` (generics spelled out in words here because GitHub strips them from PR text);
- the `ActionRunner` class gains `private dispatchCollected;`.

`@object-ui/react`'s `ActionProviderProps.onParamCollection` imports the type by name, so its bytes do not change. `ParamDialogState` gains an optional `run`, but that type is not in `@object-ui/app-shell`'s barrel. The changeset declares `@object-ui/core` minor and `@object-ui/app-shell` patch, the precedent objectui#12967 set for the third argument.

## Files beyond the claimed surface (in-place, same defect class)

- `packages/app-shell/src/views/RecordDetailView.tsx`: the second runner-fed host. Its handler forwards `run` the same way, or record-page dialogs would keep closing. `RecordDetailView.paramRuntimeParity-6431.test.tsx`'s `DIALOG_READS` gains `run`; that pin goes red when only one runtime carries the key.
- `packages/app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/MetadataTypeActions.tsx` (a comment) and `MetadataTypeActions.paramDialogClose-6473.test.tsx` (a header line): both quoted the old submit expression, which this change replaces. The census pin in that suite (two settle-then-close sites in the dialog) stays green unchanged, because `handleSubmit` keeps one close site.
- No open pull request touches any of these files (REST read of the open PRs' files at the time of writing).

## Evidence, at head `84d0fb1`

- Targeted suite: every test under `packages/core/src/actions/`, plus every `ActionParamDialog*`, `RecordDetailView.param*`, `RecordDetailView.confirmRuntimeParity*`, `useConsoleActionRuntime*` and `MetadataTypeActions*` suite in app-shell, `page-header-actions` and the `renderers/action` suites in components, and `packages/react/src/`. Result: `Test Files  222 passed (222)`, `Tests  2947 passed (2947)`.
- New pins:
  - `ActionRunner.paramRun-13161.test.ts`: 7 tests on the runner session;
  - `ActionParamDialog.refusalKeepsInput-13161.test.tsx`: 9 tests on the dialog;
  - `useConsoleActionRuntime.paramRefusal-13161.test.tsx`: one end-to-end test with a real `ActionRunner`, the console runtime's own handler and the real dialog.
- Ablation 1, the dialog. Committed fix, then `ActionParamDialog.tsx` written back to the base blob.
  - Mutation on disk: `git hash-object` `89f103a` equals the base blob, with `state.run` and `action-param-refusal` counted at 0.
  - Run: `Tests  9 failed | 1 passed (10)` across the dialog suite and the end-to-end suite. The ablation target fails at `Unable to find an element by: [data-testid="action-param-refusal"]`. The one green test is the no-`run` control, by design.
  - Restore: `git checkout HEAD --` the absolute path, then `git hash-object` `fac7fb7` equals the HEAD blob, and `git diff HEAD` is empty.
- Ablation 2, the runner. Same procedure on `ActionRunner.ts`.
  - Mutation on disk: `5778e79` equals the base blob, with `dispatchCollected` counted at 0.
  - Run: `Tests  8 failed | 6 passed (14)`. All 7 session pins and the end-to-end test fail. The 6 legacy `ActionRunner.params.test.ts` tests stay green both ways, which is the old-contract control.
  - Restore: `074b624` equals the HEAD blob, and `git diff HEAD` is empty.
- `type-check` for `@object-ui/core` and `@object-ui/app-shell`: exit 0 (both programs, `tsc --noEmit` and `tsconfig.test.json`; app-shell's test program includes every `*.test.tsx`).
- `lint` for both packages: exit 0, 0 errors.
- Each gate printed its own verdict and exited 0:
  - `pnpm check:new-line-citations`: `VERDICT new-cross-file-line-citations: 0 new citation(s)`;
  - `pnpm check:control-bytes`: OK;
  - `pnpm check:changeset-claims`: no findings;
  - `node scripts/check-changeset-presence.mjs`: 10 source files of 2 released packages, 1 changeset;
  - `node scripts/check-changeset-no-major.mjs`: OK;
  - `node scripts/check-governed-queue-guard.mjs --test` over the 11 changed paths: NOT GOVERNED.
- No user-facing string was added (the refusal is the run's own text and the busy state is a spinner), so the i18n gates were not run.

## Acceptance notes

- **Field marking has no channel.** `ActionResult` carries a refusal as text, and every console handler (`apiHandler`, core's server-action handler, the flow handler, the runner's update path) flattens the envelope's `fields` to it. A refusal whose envelope does name a field is therefore also shown as the form's. Whether to widen `ActionResult` is a question in the report, not a change made here. Carrier: none.
- **`MetadataTypeActions` still closes on Confirm.** It runs without the runner, and no metadata type's type-level action declares params today: the datasource type's `test_connection` and `migrate_credential` declare none. The path is dormant. Carrier: none.
- **A run that never settles leaves the dialog busy with Cancel disabled.** The run cannot be called back, and closing would hide its outcome, which is the defect this card fixes. The cost is accepted and stated here rather than handled.
- **The runner still toasts a refusal** while the dialog shows it, which is the object form's precedent (banner plus toast). A success toast is unchanged.
- **New `Record of string to any` spellings** in the runner and its test add `no-explicit-any` warnings. They mirror the handler's own return type. The repo sets no `--max-warnings`.
- **Out of scope, for its owner** (reported, not fixed): Users, then Create User left blank, answers "Either email or phoneNumber is required" on a form with no phone field. The `sys_user` `create_user` action declares `email` with `required: false`, because the endpoint takes email OR phone and the phone param is feature-gated. So the dialog's own "is required" check cannot fire, and the server's copy names a field the form does not show.
